name: Genetic Central Nervous System Malformation

criteria.description: Identification of structural CNS abnormalities on MRI or CT scan
Detection of pathogenic variants in genes associated with CNS malformations
Presence of neurological deficits consistent with CNS malformation
Positive family history of CNS malformations or related genetic disorders
Evidence of developmental delay or intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of CNS structural abnormalities on neuroimaging plus identification of pathogenic genetic variant and consistent neurological clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetics, neurology, and radiology.

pathognomonic.notes: Abnormal cortical development visible on imaging
Enlargement of cerebral ventricles detected by imaging

common.notes: Cognitive impairment ranging from mild to severe

occasional.notes: Accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid causing increased intracranial pressure
Impairment of one or more cranial nerves
searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

occasional.notes: Increased muscle tone with exaggerated tendon reflexes

rare.symptomName: Visual impairment due to optic nerve hypoplasia
rare.notes: Underdevelopment of the optic nerve leading to vision problems
searchTerms: poor vision from small optic nerves
optic nerve underdevelopment causing vision loss
vision problems due to optic nerve issues

rare.notes: Hearing loss due to inner ear or nerve abnormalities

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing pathogenic variants in genes such as LIS1, DCX, or ARX
imaging: MRI demonstrating cortical malformations including lissencephaly, polymicrogyria, or heterotopia
CT scan showing ventriculomegaly or hydrocephalus
genetic: Autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, or X-linked inheritance patterns depending on gene involved
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities consistent with seizure activity

distinguishingFeatures: History of prenatal or perinatal insult
Imaging findings consistent with acquired injury rather than developmental anomaly
Presence of metabolic derangements on laboratory testing
Progressive neurological decline without structural malformations

redFlags: Onset of refractory seizures in infancy
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting and bulging fontanelle
references: Orphanet: Genetic Central Nervous System Malformation - ORPHA:183506
Barkovich AJ, et al. A developmental and genetic classification for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012.
Dobyns WB, et al. Genetic malformations of the human cerebral cortex. Neurology. 2010.
